subtitle: PC LAUNCHER
tagline: The PlayStation 2 classic, now on PC.
readyDescription: Build ready. Choose your settings and return to the fight.
missing: Missing files: see the Files tab
gpuDesc: The GPU that renders the game. A dedicated card is much faster.
gpuMissing: The selected graphics card is not visible now (GPU mode may have changed); the system default will be used.
modeDesc: Can be toggled in game with F11.
fullResolution: Fullscreen uses your display's native resolution.
aspectDesc: Shape of the picture and of the window; the camera is only widened with widescreen on.
widescreenDesc: PCSX2's widescreen patch: widens the camera to the sides (Hor+) at the aspect ratio above. Off: the game's original 4:3 picture, with side bars.
aspect329Note: The camera is widened, but the HUD and menus are stretched across the whole width. The game was not made for this width, so objects may appear or vanish near the edges. A render resolution of 3× or more keeps the picture sharp.
stretchDesc: No black bars, but proportions are distorted.
scalingDesc: How the game's image is fitted to your screen. If the render resolution is larger than the screen, it is downsampled by area averaging.
sharpnessDesc: Sharpening strength of the bicubic filter (0 = none).
progressiveDesc: On (default): the game's sharp 480p mode. Off: its interlaced mode with the anti-flicker filter, softer.
brightnessDesc: Lifts or lowers the whole picture. 50 = as the game draws it.
contrastDesc: Spreads or narrows the gap between dark and light around mid-grey. 50 = unchanged.
gammaDesc: Brightens (above 50) or darkens (below 50) the mid-tones while keeping black and white. Helps a dark game on PC monitors.
saturationDesc: Color intensity: 0 = black and white, 50 = unchanged, 100 = vivid.
imageResetDesc: Puts the four sliders back at 50: the picture exactly as the game draws it.
internalDesc: Multiple of the native resolution, up to 8×. 2× is recommended; above it the game gets heavier for the graphics card.
scaleWarning: At 3× the game no longer holds 60 fps on mid-range cards, and 4× to 8× need a powerful GPU. If the fps drops, go back to 2×.
internalUnstable4x: Experimental · may stall or run slowly in heavy scenes
fallbackSmoothnessDesc: Uses 2× automatically when 3× is selected. Recommended for stable 60 FPS in heavy scenes.
fpsLimitDesc: The game's real frame rate. 60 is the PS2's own; 120 is the highest. The game keeps its normal speed at either limit: more FPS only makes it smoother.
vsyncDesc: Prevents tearing by locking to the display refresh rate. Not recommended for this game: it can cause stutter.
vsyncWarning: When a frame misses the display refresh, VSync holds it back until the next one: the picture stutters and the controls feel delayed. For smooth play, leave VSync off and let the FPS limit pace the game.
showFpsDesc: Shows the game's real frame rate in the corner of the screen.
showGpuDesc: GPU usage and temperature, video memory used and memory clock, when the system reports them.
earlyFinishDesc: The game prepares the next frame while the current one is still being drawn. More frames per second in heavy scenes and above 60 FPS; turn it off only to compare or if something looks wrong.
noteFps: Above 60 the game runs more frames per second without speeding up: movement, timers and sound keep their normal pace. If the PC cannot reach the limit, it simply shows fewer frames. The window always refreshes at the monitor's rate. Some actions timed in frames (quick-time events, combo windows) may feel slightly different; go back to 60 if anything seems off. The heaviest scenes are CPU-bound.
elfDesc: The main PS2 program from the disc. Game data is looked up in the same folder.
elfInvalid: This file is not God of War NTSC-U (CRC %1)
errorElfMismatch: ELF does not match this build.
isoDesc: Optional. If empty, the .iso in the game folder is used.
extractedIso: Extracted game files will be used
isoMissing: No disc image or extracted game files found
chosenIsoMissing: The selected ISO was not found
memoryDesc: Memory card image (Mcd001.ps2) that holds all your saved games. Back up this file to keep your saves.
cancelAnimationsDesc: Cuts the end of a roll short with an attack or block and briefly remembers missed attack presses. Cancelling attacks with block and evade is already in the game.
escQuitsDesc: When off, quit by closing the window.
cheatsNotice: During the game, F2 opens the cheat menu and toggles cheats instantly. The ones here are active when the game starts.
cheatsShortcut: Gamepad shortcut for the cheat menu
cheatsShortcutDesc: F2 always works. Capture one button or hold two buttons together; either opens the in-game extras menu.
cheatsShortcutCapturing: Release the pad, then press one button or two together…
cheatsShortcutUnavailable: Gamepad capture is only available on Windows right now.
cheatsShortcutFailed: No supported gamepad button was captured.
cheat_god_modeDesc: Kratos takes no damage; health stays full.
cheat_one_hit_killDesc: Enemies and bosses die in a single hit.
cheat_infinite_rageDesc: Rage meter always full; never runs out while active.
cheat_all_upgradesDesc: Blades of Chaos level 5; magic and Blade of Artemis level 3.
cheat_all_powersDesc: Zeus's Fury, Medusa's Gaze, Poseidon's Rage, Army of Hades, Blade of Artemis and Poseidon's Trident.
cheat_max_metersDesc: Every Gorgon Eye and Phoenix Feather upgrade.
cheat_unlock_extrasDesc: God Mode difficulty, costumes, videos and Challenge of the Gods. Permanent once you save.
keyboardDesc: Click a key, then press the new key or click a mouse button. Right-click clears it. Each action can have two keys.
padSchemeDesc: PS2 layout by default; modern layout is optional.
padButtonDesc: PS2 button sent to the game; an existing assignment is swapped automatically.
captureDesc: Press a key or click a mouse button for %1. Cancel: Esc
conflict: This key is also used by: %1
reservedNotice: This key is used in game for fullscreen (F11), the cheat menu (F2) or the developer panel (F1).
skipVideosDesc: Skips the game's pre-rendered videos (e.g. the intro).
fastBootDesc: Cuts the intro animation short; the opening scene and lines may be cut. Not recommended.
minimizeOnPlayDesc: It comes back when the game closes.
shortcutsDesc: Open the launcher from the app menu or the desktop.
logDesc: Check this file if something goes wrong.
resetDesc: Resets graphics and performance settings; file paths are kept.
aboutText: God of War is a trademark of Sony Interactive Entertainment. This port contains no game files; you need your own copy.
errorExecutable: The port runner is missing or not executable.
errorElf: The game executable (SCUS_973.99) was not found.
raSummary: Enables RetroAchievements. The ISO is optional: without it, the game is identified from the original SCUS_973.99 executable.
raEnabledDesc: Signs in and loads the achievement set when the game starts.
raPasswordDesc: Save only stores the password in the Windows Credential Manager. Sign-in happens when the game starts.
raPasswordSaved: Password saved in the Windows Credential Manager. Sign-in happens when the game starts.
raHardcoreDesc: Cheats are disabled. Required for hardcore achievements.
raNotificationsDesc: Shows a notification in the game when an achievement is unlocked.
raIsoDesc: Neither the ISO nor the SCUS_973.99 in this install is the original (modified or translated): RetroAchievements will not recognize the game.
raIsoOk: The game is identified by the original ISO's hash.
raIsoElf: The original SCUS_973.99 is used to identify the game.
optimizationEnabledDesc: Recompiles the game with the new parts you reach, so it keeps getting faster. The data stays on your PC.
optimizeDuringGameDesc: Turns rebuilding on with the game open. It competes for the CPU and freezes the picture for tens of seconds; off (the default), it only runs after you close the game.
optimizeDuringGameWarning: The rebuild uses every core: with the game open it stops receiving frames and the picture freezes. Turn it on only when debugging.
wizStep1Title: Choose your God of War ISO
wizStep1Text: The installer looks for your original God of War (USA, SCUS-97399) ISO, or a CHD of it, on this PC. If it does not find it, drop the file here or click Browse. The ISO is verified: the original disc works, and so does a disc modified without changing the game's code (a translation, an undub, a texture mod). An .xdelta patch can be applied to the original below. Nothing leaves your computer.
wizSearchingHint: This takes a few seconds. You can also drop the file here.
wizDragHint: or click Browse to choose it.
wizIsoFound: Found automatically · original ISO verified (USA, SCUS-97399).
wizStep2Hint: This folder holds the extracted game files and the compiled build. The ISO is not needed afterwards.
wizRamLimit4: Limit the installer to 4 GB of RAM
wizRamLimit4Desc: Recommended. Keeps the VU1 optimization and compiler concurrency conservative.
wizRamLimit8: Limit the installer to 8 GB of RAM
wizRamLimit8Desc: Uses a larger VU1 optimization set while still leaving headroom for Windows.
wizSummaryText: Everything is set. Review and click Install; the rest happens on its own.
wizSummaryTimeVal: about 10 to 20 minutes on Windows; longer on older PCs and on Linux
wizConfirmCancel: Cancel the installation? What was already done is kept, so you can resume later.
wizErrorHint: Try again: the finished steps are skipped. The installation log has the full details.
wizIsoPlaceholder: Path to the ISO or CHD file
wizIsoUnreadable: The file could not be read.
wizIsoFormat: This does not look like a PS2 DVD ISO (2048 bytes per sector).
wizIsoOtherGame: This ISO is not God of War (USA, SCUS-97399).
wizIsoNoExe: The game executable was not found in the ISO.
wizIsoModified: This ISO is modified or a different edition (hash %1). It needs the original USA ISO, or a translation that kept the game's code.
wizStep2Text: Choose the folder for the extracted game files and the recompiled build. Use a path without accents.
wizDestinationCharacters: The path cannot contain accents or special characters.
wizDestinationSpace: Not enough space: %1 GB free; at least 20 GB are needed.
wizComponentsDesc: Tick what the installer should download. All of these are required to compile the game.
wizComponentsOk: All the required components are already installed.
wizCompVsDesc: Microsoft's C++ compiler. Downloaded from Microsoft under its license; Windows asks for administrator permission and it takes 15 to 30 minutes.
wizCompGitDesc: Downloads the project libraries (raylib, imgui...). Stays inside the install folder; nothing is installed in Windows.
wizNoInstaller: The installer script (install.ps1 on Windows, install.sh on Linux) was not found next to the repository. Run the launcher from the project folder.
wizLinuxMissingDesc: The build needs programs and libraries that this system does not have yet. The launcher cannot install them for you because that needs your password: run the command below in a terminal, then press Check again.
wizLinuxUnknown: This distribution is not recognized, so there is no command to offer. Install the equivalents of cmake, ninja, a C++ compiler, git, pkg-config and the development files of GL, X11, Xrandr, Xinerama, Xcursor, Xi, xkbcommon, Wayland and ALSA, then press Check again.
wizCompilingText: This takes a while (about 10 to 20 minutes on Windows; longer on older PCs and on Linux). You can leave the launcher open; do not turn the computer off.
wizOptimizationNotice: During the optimization step the game opens by itself for a few minutes: do not touch the keyboard or controller.
wizCancelled: Installation canceled. You can compile again; finished steps are skipped.
wizSuccessText: The game was compiled successfully. Click OK to go to the launcher.
wizErrorText: The installation stopped with an error:
raHardcoreCheatsNotice: RetroAchievements Hardcore is on: cheats are not sent to the game.
customTexturesDesc: Draws the texture replacements you put in the textures folder (PCSX2 format: .png or .dds files named by hash). Takes effect the next time the game starts.
texturesFolderDesc: Opens the textures folder of the installation. Put the pack inside its "replacements" folder, as in PCSX2.
texturesNeedGame: Choose the game files first: the textures folder is created next to them.
texturePackNeedsGame: Install the game first: the texture pack is installed inside its folder.
texturePackDesc: Downloads the community pack (%1 GB) and replaces everything in textures/replacements with it. The folder you have now is only swapped once the pack is fully extracted, so a failed install keeps it, and the ZIP is deleted afterwards. The card disappears once the pack is installed.
texturePackBusy: Installing the texture pack. This takes several minutes: keep this tab and the launcher open until it finishes.
texturePackLocked: The texture pack is being installed. Wait until it finishes before leaving this tab.
texturePackCloseTitle: The texture pack is still installing
texturePackCloseText: If you close the launcher now, the download is lost and has to start again. The textures you have now are not touched. Close anyway?
texturePackFailed: The texture pack could not be installed
asyncTexturesDesc: Reads the replacements in the background and draws the game's own texture until each one is ready, spreading the work on the GPU so the game does not stutter. Off waits for every file (each new texture may pause the game briefly).
updateInstalling: Installing the update, the launcher will restart
updatePortableNote: This portable copy cannot update itself: download the new zip from the release page.
updateManualNote: Download it from the release page.
updateBlocked_optimizer: Wait for the optimization to finish.
updateBlocked_texturePack: Wait for the texture pack to install.
autoUpdateDesc: Checks for a new version of the launcher at start-up and installs it by itself when the game, the installer and the optimization are idle, then restarts the launcher. Off: you only see a notice and press Update. A portable copy only shows the notice.
wizCpuUnsupported: This PC's processor does not support SSE4.1, which the game needs (Intel Core 2 'Penryn' from 2008 or newer, AMD 'Bulldozer' from 2011 or newer). The game cannot run here, so the installation is blocked.
failureKitFile: A file of the installation kit is missing, most likely removed by an antivirus. Close the launcher and open it again to restore it. If it keeps happening, add the launcher's data folder to your antivirus exclusions.
failureKitMissing: Installation kit files are missing: %1. Close the launcher and open it again to restore them. If they stay missing, extract the launcher's zip again (portable copy) or add the launcher's data folder to your antivirus exclusions.
failureCmakeUnusable: The installer could not find a CMake that can build the game (version 3.21 or newer, with cmcldeps.exe). Try again with an Internet connection, so it can download a portable one, or install Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools.
failureDownload: A download failed. Check the Internet connection and that no firewall or antivirus is blocking the launcher, then try again.
failureOpenGl: The graphics driver could not provide the OpenGL context the game needs. Update the graphics driver. A remote desktop session or the Microsoft Basic Display Adapter cannot run the game.
failureMissingDll: Windows could not find a library the game needs (error code 0xC0000135). Run the installation again, and check that no antivirus removed files from the game folder.
failureBadImage: Windows could not load the game or one of its libraries, because the file is damaged or built for another kind of PC (error code 0xC000007B). Run the installation again on this PC.
rebuildNoteTitle: Rebuild the game to get the latest fixes
rebuildNoteText: Fixes for the game were installed with this update. Rebuild the game to get them. It takes from a few minutes to about 20 minutes; you can keep using the current build until then.
rebuildToast: Fixes for the game came with this update. Open Performance to rebuild the game.
playRebuildPausesText: A rebuild of the game is running in the background. If you open the game now, the rebuild is paused so the two do not compete for the processor and the picture does not freeze. It starts again when you close the game, and what was already compiled is kept.
playRebuildKeepsText: A rebuild of the game is running in the background. With "Also while playing" on, it keeps running while you play, so the game can stutter or freeze until it finishes.
rebuildStarted: Rebuilding the game in the background.
rebuildDone: The game was rebuilt. The new version opens the next time you play.
rebuildFailedTitle: The last rebuild of the game failed
rebuildFailedText: The game was not rebuilt, so the previous build keeps working. Try again later; if it fails again, open the log of the rebuild and attach it to an issue.
rebuildFailedToast: The rebuild of the game failed. Open Performance for the details.
rebuildUnavailable: The game could not be rebuilt: the installation folder was not found.
rebuildBlocked_optimizer: Wait for the optimization to finish.
rebuildBlocked_texturePack: Wait for the texture pack to install.
presetDesc: Sets the render resolution, upscaling filter and anti-aliasing together. It changes how heavy the picture is for your graphics card, not the speed of the game itself.
reportExportDesc: Saves a ZIP with the launcher's logs, your settings and details of this PC, with your user name and folders removed, to attach to a bug report on GitHub. Game files and saves are never included.
reportFailed: The report could not be saved.
reportMarkDesc: A short note on what went wrong, for example where in the game. It goes into the next report. Do not write personal information.
padmapDesc: Which PS2 button each button of your gamepad presses. The first change starts from the layout you have now. A button set to Nothing does nothing.
padmapLocked: Set by the custom button map below.
padmapSharedTitle: Two buttons press the same PS2 button
padmapShared: %1 is pressed by more than one button. That works, but check it is what you want.
padmapNoStart: Start must stay on one of the buttons, or the game cannot be started. That change was not applied.
padpickDesc: Which device the game reads. Automatic uses the first controller that answers. The list is what the game saw the last time it ran.
padpickNone: No controller has been seen yet. Start the game once with the controller connected and it will be listed here.
padpickUnmappedTitle: The system has no button layout for this device
padpickUnmappedText: The game would see every button of %1 as released. This is common with generic 2.4G receivers. Map its buttons yourself, pick another device from the list, or play with the keyboard.
padpickAbsent: The device you chose was not connected the last time the game ran, so the game picked a pad by itself.
padpickOutOfRange: The device you chose was past the first four the game can read the last time it ran, so the game picked a pad by itself.
padsdlIntro: The system has no button layout for this controller, so you describe it here. Start the game with the controller connected (the keyboard works in the menus), then come back and press Listen next to a button. The game reports which input moved, in the numbering it uses itself. The mapping takes effect the next time you start the game.
padsdlWaiting: Waiting for the game. Start it with this controller connected and keep this window open.
padsdlMissing: The game is running but does not list this controller. Check that it is plugged in.
padsdlListening: Press or move %1 on the controller. Esc cancels.
padsdlNeedStart: Map Start before saving: without it the game cannot be started.
padsdlShared: %1 use an input that another button uses too. That works, but check it.
padsdlInUse: A hand-made button layout is set for this controller. It applies the next time you start the game.
profileOfferDesc: Up to about 13% more FPS in combat. Takes about 15 minutes: the game opens by itself for 4 minutes and then the game is rebuilt. PLAY stays locked until it finishes.
profileRunningDesc: Optimizing: follow the steps in the window in front. PLAY stays locked until it finishes.
profileReadyDesc: Active: this installation was optimized on this PC.
profileStarted: Optimizing: the game will open by itself. Do not use the PC for about 15 minutes.
profileUnavailable: This installation cannot be optimized this way (it needs the Windows build made with clang).
buildWorkingCores: Working: the build is using %1 processor cores right now.
buildWorkingCore: Working: the build is using %1% of one processor core right now.
buildWaiting: Not using the processor at this moment (for %1). Short pauses between steps are normal.
buildStuck: No processor use and no output for %1: it may be stuck. Open the log; if it stays like this, close the launcher (that stops the build) and start it again.
buildCpuUnknown: The processor use of the build cannot be read on this system; the last output below shows what it did last.
buildDownloading: Downloading: this step waits on your internet connection, so the processor stays quiet. A slow connection only makes it longer.
buildStepTranslate: Translating the game's code to C++
buildStepVu1: Reading the VU1 microcode from the game
buildStepInstrumented: Building the test version of the game
buildStepTraining: The game is open by itself recording the profile
buildQuietHint: Some steps print nothing until they finish: generating the native VU1 code and linking the game can take up to about 30 minutes each. While the line at the top says it is working, it is.
profileConfirmIntro: It takes about 15 minutes, in three steps:
profileStepBuilding: A test version of the game is built
profileStepBuildingHint: You can use the PC normally.
profileStepTraining: The game opens by itself for about 4 minutes
profileStepTrainingHint: Do not touch the keyboard, mouse or controller and do not close the game window: it plays and closes by itself.
profileStepFinishingHint: You can use the PC, but do not open the game.
profileConfirmRules: PLAY stays locked until the end. Do not close the launcher meanwhile: that stops the optimization halfway.
profileTrainingWarningTitle: The game opened by itself: hands off
profileTrainingWarning: Do not touch the keyboard, mouse or controller and do not close the game window. It closes by itself in about 4 minutes.
profileOverlayFoot: PLAY stays locked until the optimization finishes. Closing the launcher stops it halfway.
profileCancelConfirm: Cancel the optimization? Its game closes, and if the test version was already built the game is rebuilt the normal way (a few minutes, with PLAY locked meanwhile).
profileCloseText: If you close the launcher now, the optimization stops halfway. The next time the launcher opens it rebuilds the game the normal way before you can play. Close anyway?
instrumentedChip: Slow test version installed: PLAY locked
instrumentedDesc: An optimization was interrupted and left its test version of the game, which runs several times slower. The launcher rebuilds the game by itself; PLAY comes back when it finishes.
errorProfiling: The optimization is running and opens the game by itself: wait for it to finish.
errorInstrumented: This is the slow test version left by an interrupted optimization, so it does not open. The launcher is rebuilding the game; PLAY comes back when it finishes.
failureDamagedDisc: The game disc image is damaged or incomplete (a download or copy that stopped early). Make the ISO again from your original disc and choose it again.
failureCompilerSetup: The compiler could not be downloaded. Check the Internet connection and that no firewall or antivirus is blocking github.com, then try again; finished steps are kept.
failureBuildFolderCompiler: The build folder is still set up for another compiler. Delete the file CMakeCache.txt in the installation's build folder and try again.
raOtherEdition: Achievements only work with the original God of War (USA) disc. The game installed here comes from another edition or a modified disc (a translation or a mod): it plays normally, but RetroAchievements stays off.
wizIsoTranslation: Modified disc recognized (a translation, an undub or a data mod): same code as the USA game, so it installs and plays normally. RetroAchievements only work with the original disc.
wizIsoOtherEdition: This is God of War (%1), an edition the port does not support yet: it has its own code. Use the USA disc (SCUS-97399) or a translation of it.
rebuildLegacyTitle: Rebuild the game from scratch for 0.3.0
rebuildLegacyText: This game was compiled by version 0.2.9 or older, with Visual Studio. Version 0.3.0 compiles it with a new compiler (clang), so the old build is deleted and the game is compiled again from scratch: about 10 to 20 minutes, plus a 170 MB download the first time. Until it ends you can keep playing the current version; if it fails, the old build is put back.
rebuildLegacySaves: Your saves and the memory card (game/Mcd001.ps2) are not part of the build and are not touched.
rebuildLegacyToast: This game was compiled by 0.2.9 or older. Open Performance to rebuild it from scratch for 0.3.0 (your saves stay).
wizPatchDesc: A translation, an undub or another mod distributed as an .xdelta patch. Creates a patched copy of this ISO in the same folder and installs that one; the original ISO is not changed.
wizPatchHint: Choose the .xdelta file of the patch.
wizPatchWillCreate: Creates %1 in the same folder (about 8 GB).
wizPatchOriginalKept: The installation uses this patched ISO. The original ISO was not changed.
wizPatchPending: Apply the patch, or untick the option, to continue.
wizPatchError_patch-unreadable: The patch file could not be read.
wizPatchError_not-xdelta: This file is not an xdelta patch.
wizPatchError_compressed: This patch uses a compression the launcher cannot read. Ask for a version made with "xdelta3 -S none".
wizPatchError_wrong-iso: This patch was made for a different ISO, not for the original USA disc.
wizPatchError_damaged: The patch is damaged or incomplete. Download it again.
wizPatchError_space: Not enough free space in the ISO’s folder for the patched copy (about 8 GB).
wizPatchError_changes-code: This patch changes the game’s executable (code patches such as widescreen hacks, cheats or fixes). The port runs the USA disc’s own code, so it cannot use it. Nothing was kept.
wizPatchError_write: The patched ISO could not be written. Check the folder’s permissions and free space.
wizIsoChd: This CHD cannot be read: it is damaged, an old CHD version, a delta that needs its parent CHD, or it uses an unknown compression. Use a complete CHD made by a recent chdman, or the ISO.
wizChdOk: CHD image: original disc verified inside it (USA, SCUS-97399).
wizChdFound: Found automatically · CHD image with the original disc (USA, SCUS-97399).
wizChdTitle: CHD image: converted to ISO before installing
wizChdWillCreate: Writes %1 (%2 GB) in the CHD’s folder. The CHD is not changed. Takes about a minute.
wizChdExisting: Already converted: %1 is in the CHD’s folder and will be used.
wizChdSpace: Not enough free space in the CHD’s folder for the ISO: %1 GB needed, %2 GB free.
wizChdKept: The installation uses this ISO. Your CHD was not changed.
wizChdError_unreadable: This CHD cannot be read (an old version, a delta of another CHD, or an unknown compression).
wizChdError_damaged: The CHD is damaged or incomplete: part of it does not match its checksum. Download or copy it again. Nothing was created.
wizChdError_space: Not enough free space in the CHD’s folder for the ISO (about 8 GB).
wizChdError_not-game: The disc inside this CHD is not a God of War (USA) the port can install. Nothing was kept.
wizChdError_write: The ISO could not be written. Check the folder’s permissions and free space.
